profile.reading: This is Retelits Avalon 3 data center at Via Bisceglie 95 in Milan, Italy, about 4 kilometers from the Avalon 1 building, offering about 3.2 megawatts of IT power across more than 3,500 square meters, or roughly 37,700 square feet, of floor space, with ground floor load capacity rated to 1,500 kilograms per square meter. The facility is certified to ANSI/TIA-942 Rating 4, holds Uptime Institute Tier IV certification for 99.99 percent uptime, ISO 22237 certification, and LEED v4 Gold certification, operating at a reported power usage effectiveness of about 1.3 on a claimed 100 percent renewable electricity supply. Avalon 3 is positioned as part of what Retelit calls Italys largest internet exchange point and most interconnected data center campus, interconnecting more than 170 carriers and cloud providers together with the neighboring Avalon 1 and Avalon 2 buildings to function as a single virtual campus data center with direct access to Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, and Amazon Web Services. Starting in 2026, Avalon 3s waste heat is set to feed Milans district heating network, managed by utility A2A, supplying an estimated 2.5 megawatts of thermal power annually, enough to heat about 1,250 homes, in what Retelit describes as Italys first data center heat recovery project. Retelit traces its roots to 1996 as e-Planet, listed on Borsa Italianas main market in 2000, and built its core business around fiber optic data transmission, reporting more than 43,000 kilometers of fiber network and 34 data centers nationwide, including participation in the AAE-1 international submarine cable consortium. The company delisted from the stock exchange on November 29, 2021 after Asterion Industrial Partners tender offer exceeded 95 percent acceptance, and Asterion now owns 100 percent of Retelit, which has separately announced a 100 million euro investment in two additional AI ready data centers within the same Milan Bisceglie complex.
